investigator.method: Bounded, single unauthenticated Level-1 PASSIVE_STATIC GET (curl, descriptive User-Agent, redirects followed, 20s timeout, no retry, no authentication, no CAPTCHA/challenge bypass, no browser) against the venue's official_website (falling back to official_programme_url where noted), as part of BEATMAPPED-LONDON-SECOND-LIVE-TRANCHE-01 batch 6 of 7.

probe_history.reason: A single unauthenticated Level-1 static GET against https://sohoplace.org/whats-on/ retained enough real evidence (event/programme listing content, title/meta tags, and structured data where present) to reach an honest, evidenced REJECT decision without needing to escalate to Level 2/3/4.

identity.notes: The retained page's own <title> ('What's On at @sohoplace | London Theatre Shows & Events') and meta description directly self-identify the domain as @sohoplace's official What's On page.

site_classification.platform: Server-rendered static HTML 'site-event-card' markup (no JSON-LD Event schema observed in this bounded probe).

venue_location.notes: Discovery evidence reports Soho Place 4, W1D 3BG, London; the retained page did not itself restate a street address in this bounded excerpt.

reasons: The retained event-card excerpt and surrounding page show @sohoplace's current and recent programme is entirely West-End style theatre productions: 'Tao of Glass' (a theatre piece described as a 'West End premiere' blending meditations with music, presented as a play, not a concert), 'Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?', 'The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind', 'Marie & Rosetta', and 'The Spy Who Came In From The Cold'.

The page's own meta description self-identifies the venue's offering as 'a diverse lineup of performances, from drama to musicals' — book-musicals/plays, not live concerts — matching the policy's guidance that @sohoplace is a West-End style theatre likely to be rejected absent real evidence of substantially live-music/concert programming, which this probe did not find.

evidence.description: Retained, bounded, genuine excerpts (contiguous literal substrings) of the actual HTTP response body from a single unauthenticated GET, plus response metadata (status/content-type/title); JSON wrapper around literal excerpt strings, so not byte-faithful as a whole file.
evidence.method: curl -L (redirects followed); descriptive User-Agent; unauthenticated GET; 20-second timeout; no retry; no browser/JS execution.
